title: Timing Constant Verification
principle: Librarium is canonical; external repos and screenshots are evidence only.

claims.claim: MajorMUD uses a 3.0-second system/spell tick for regen, buffs, debuffs, or spell duration processing.

support.detail: Changelog states bless calculations were changed to use 3-second round ticks instead of 5.
Simulator code rotates spell duration tick counters through a repeating 1..3 cadence and decrements spell duration on tick processing.
Screenshots claim 1 System Tick = 3.0 seconds and describe a global heartbeat/tick clipping model.

limitations: No primary MajorMUD/Worldgroup SDK page was provided in this package.
MBBSEmu exposes host seconds/TIMER/TICKER behavior but does not itself prove a MajorMUD 3-second gameplay tick.
MMUD Explorer is reverse-engineering/tooling evidence, not canonical Classic truth.
claims.promotion_decision: Do not promote to Verified; keep as derived candidate with high priority for trace/runtime confirmation.

claims.claim: MajorMUD uses a 1.5-second combat round and 1 tick = 2 combat rounds.

support.detail: Screenshots claim 1 Combat Round = 1.5 seconds and 1 Tick = 2 Rounds.

conflicting_or_nonconfirming_evidence.detail: Comment says SPELL ROUND = 3s, COMBAT ROUND 5s, every 3 rounds = extra spell round; adjacent comments refer to 15 seconds at three ticks.
MBBSEmu confirms host timer mechanisms and seconds counters but no attached source line confirms 1.5-second MajorMUD combat rounds.

claims.promotion_decision: Do not promote; create explicit conflict/gap requiring MegaMUD source, Classic logs, SDK documentation, or direct gameplay trace.

claims.claim: Spell/buff true duration clips against a hidden global heartbeat depending on cast time relative to the next tick.

support.detail: Screenshots describe maximum/minimum duration windows based on global tick position.

limitations: No primary source or executable trace in the current package proves cast-time clipping.
Needs a probe with timestamped cast event, global tick event, duration decrement, and expiration.
claims.promotion_decision: Do not promote; add runtime trace probe requirement.

claims.claim: MBBSEmu host exposes second-based and timer-based scheduling primitives that support host-driven timing rather than client/modem-driven simulation.

support.detail: TICKER variable is allocated and updated from elapsed seconds once per second.
Host has Timer.Hertz-driven timer events, in-module STSROU/STTROU/polling handling, and real-time processing calls RTKICK/RTIHDLR/SYSCYC/Tasks.

claims.promotion_decision: Keep as observed MBBSEmu host behavior; not enough to verify Classic MajorMUD constants.
